messages.subject: ctmm.fit VS ctmm.select
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I am just starting using the ctmm package and I am confused about the difference between the ctmm.fit and ctmm.select fonction.
My understanding is that the ctmm.select use the results of a ctmm.guess (for the sake of this example) to fit various models on the data and then ranks them based on their AICc values.
But which model does the ctmm.fit does fit based on the same ctmm.guess object?

Thanks for the help!

Stephanie

messages.subject: Re: ctmm.fit VS ctmm.select
messages.body_plain:
Hi Stephanie,

ctmm.fit() returns a model of the same class as the guess argument. By default from ctmm.guess(), this is an OUF model with anisotropic covariance.

There are some other examples in the MEE Application paper: https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/2041-210X.12559

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: akde overlap
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I am now trying to look at the overlap between UDs computed using different correlation models.
Here is what I do :
data(buffalo)
## Fit the model and AKDE with NO correlation
M.IID <- lapply(buffalo[1:2], function(b) ctmm.fit(b) )
lkde <- akde(buffalo[1:2],M.IID)
# Fit the model and AKDE with  correlation
guessb <- lapply(buffalo[1:2], function(b) ctmm.guess(b,interactive=FALSE) )

models <- list()
for(i.indiv in seq(1, 2)) {
     indiv.id <http://indiv.id> <- buffalo[[i.indiv]]@info$identity
     cat(sprintf("Fitting & selecting model for %s\n", indiv.id <http://indiv.id>))
     # find best model based on AICc (default)
     models[[indiv.id <http://indiv.id>]] <- ctmm.select(buffalo[[i.indiv]], CTMM  = guess[[i.indiv]], verbose = TRUE, level   = 1, method  = "pHREML")[[1]]
}

akde <- akde(buffalo[1:2],models)

And now I would like to run the following:
overlap(c(lkde,akde) which gives me  Error in object[[1]]$PDF * object[[2]]$PDF : non-conformable arrays
 overlap(lkde) and overlap(akde) work just fine.

How can I solve this problem?
I assume this could be solved by adding the same grid argument to both lkde <- akde(buffalo[1:2],M.IID, grid=X) and akde <- akde(buffalo[1:2],models,gird=X) but since grid is not yet supported (I'm using ctmm version0.5.2) , what could be a work around?

Thank you!

Stephanie

messages.body_plain:
Replying to myself here as I think I found a work around. Is the following correct (using the same objects sales as before)?
o <- akde(c(buffalo,buffalo),c(M.IID,models))# compute KDE and AKDE
overlap.CIs <- overlap(o, debias=TRUE)#compute overlap between pairs

This proceeds UDs on the same grid for both KDEs and AKDEs and the overlap function has no problem dealing with these.

Let me know what you think.

Thanks!
Stephanie

messages.subject: Re: akde overlap
messages.body_plain:
Hi Stephanie,

This is the right way. Previously you calculated lkde on one grid and akde on a different grid, so the overlap function could only work within the two groups of UDs. This way, you calculated everything on the same grid, so you can compare across models.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Retaining individual ids when simulating multiple individuals' paths
messages.subject_clean: Retaining individual ids when simulating multiple individuals' paths
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

I have a telemetry object of multiple individuals. I am using a CTMM fit to one individual to simulate tracks across all individuals, as they all have very similar movement patterns. Is there a way to retain the individual ids from the telemetry object in the simulated tracks? So far the id slot for each simulated track is given the same id, which is the single id from the CTMM object. Here is an abbreviated example:

length(telemdata)
#165 individuals

#fit CTMM model to first individual
mod <- ctmm.select(telemdata[[1]],GUESS)
mod@info$identity
#individual identify of 'mod' CTMM object is "01"

#simulate paths with hourly intervals for each individual in telemdata
sim_paths <- lapply(telemdata, function(x) simulate(mod, data = x, dt=3600, complete = TRUE))

#for all i's
sim_paths[[i]]@info$identity
# = "01"

I'd like each simulated track to be matched with the appropriate id from telemdata/telemetry object rather than from the CTMM object.

Can this be fixed?

Thanks,
Briana

messages.subject: Re: Plotting issue with add=TRUE
messages.body_plain:
Hi Briana,

Have you tried just putting the telemetry objects in a list, with top object last? You should be able to assign colors and style arguments as a vector.

I'd started some code changes in plot.telemetry for eventually having maps/rasters as a base layer, so that's what changed. From my testing, you can still plot ctmm objects atop non-ctmm objects with add=TRUE, which is what I initially intended that argument for. I didn't think about plotting ctmm objects atop ctmm objects, which is already supported via listed arguments, but I can figure something out if that is necessary.

Best,
Chris

Hi Briana,

I think if the two objects (ctmm & telemetry) have conflicting identities, then I should probably paste them together to not discard the information. I can put that in the next update tomorrow-ish.

If you don't like that, you should be able to do something like

sim_paths <- lapply(telemdata, function(x) { TEL <- simulate(mod, data = x, dt=3600, complete = TRUE) ; TEL@info <- x@info ; return(TEL) } )

to force the identity you want.

Best,
Chris

messages.body_plain:
Hi Briana,

If sim_paths and telemdata are lists of telemetry objects, then c(sim_paths, telemdata) is a list of telemetry objects, which is what you want for ctmm functions.
If you did list(sim_paths, telemdata), then that would be a list of lists of telemetry objects... which I did not code for because telemetry objects are already based on lists and I didn't want to make trouble with that.

Best,
Chris
